title: A Rainy Day Cooking Class（雨天的烹飪課）
passage:
On Wednesday afternoon, it was raining heavily, so Mia and her friend Jack could not have basketball practice outside. Instead, their teacher, Ms. Lin, invited them to join a cooking class in the school kitchen. Although Jack had never cooked before, he decided to try making dumplings for the first time.
Ms. Lin showed the students how to mix flour and water to make the dough. She explained that the dough must rest for twenty minutes before it becomes soft enough to roll out. While waiting, Mia practiced chopping cabbage and carrots into small pieces. She enjoyed cutting the vegetables carefully because she didn't want to hurt her fingers.
When the dough was ready, Jack rolled it into thin circles. At first, his circles were not round at all, but he kept trying and slowly improved. "You might become a great chef someday," Mia said with a smile. Jack laughed and admitted that cooking was harder than he expected.
After they finished filling and folding the dumplings, Ms. Lin steamed them in a large pot. The delicious smell quickly filled the kitchen. Although the dumplings looked a little strange, they tasted amazing. Everyone agreed that Jack's dumplings, though not perfect, were the tastiest ones in the class.
Before leaving, Mia decided to bring some dumplings home for her family. She couldn't wait to tell her parents about the fun rainy afternoon she spent learning to cook.

vocab.example: It was raining heavily all afternoon.
They could not play outside, so they stayed inside instead.
Ms. Lin showed the students how to make the dough.
Mia helped chop the carrots into small pieces.
She cut the vegetables carefully so she wouldn't hurt her fingers.
Jack's dumpling shapes slowly improved after practice.
Jack admitted that cooking was harder than he expected.
Ms. Lin steamed the dumplings in a large pot.
They finished filling and folding the dumplings together.
The dumplings tasted amazing even though they looked strange.
Mia decided to bring some dumplings home for her family.
Mia joked that Jack might become a great chef someday.

grammar: 動名詞 vs. 不定詞作受詞 (Gerund vs. Infinitive as Object)：enjoy / practice / finish 等動詞後接 V-ing（動名詞）；decide / want / plan 等動詞後接 to + 原形動詞（不定詞）。例如：Mia enjoyed cutting the vegetables carefully.（enjoy + V-ing）；Jack decided to try making dumplings for the first time.（decide + to V）；They finished filling and folding the dumplings.（finish + V-ing）。

although 引導讓步子句 (Although + 子句)：表示「雖然…」，用來連接兩個對比的意思，although 子句可放句首或句中，逗號後接主要子句。例如：Although Jack had never cooked before, he decided to try.；Although the dumplings looked a little strange, they tasted amazing.

情態動詞表可能性 (could / might)：could 常表示過去的能力或可能性，用於否定句時表示「（過去）不能」；might 表示現在或未來「或許」的可能性，語氣比 may 更不確定，其後皆接原形動詞。例如：Mia and Jack could not have basketball practice outside.；You might become a great chef someday.

reading.q: Why couldn't Mia and Jack have basketball practice outside?
reading.ex: 文中提到 it was raining heavily, so Mia and her friend Jack could not have basketball practice outside，答案是 B。

reading.q: Who invited Mia and Jack to join the cooking class?
reading.ex: 文中提到 their teacher, Ms. Lin, invited them to join a cooking class，答案是 C。

reading.q: How long must the dough rest before it can be rolled out?
reading.ex: 文中提到 the dough must rest for twenty minutes before it becomes soft enough to roll out，答案是 C。

reading.q: What did Mia practice while waiting for the dough?
reading.ex: 文中提到 Mia practiced chopping cabbage and carrots into small pieces，答案是 B。

reading.q: What did Mia decide to do before leaving the cooking class?
opts: Ask Ms. Lin for the recipe
Wash all the pots and pans
Bring some dumplings home for her family
Sign up for another cooking class
reading.ex: 文末提到 Mia decided to bring some dumplings home for her family，答案是 C。

grammar.ex: enjoy 後面須接動名詞（V-ing）作受詞，故選 cutting。

grammar.q: Jack decided ___ dumplings for the first time.
grammar.ex: decide 後面須接不定詞（to + 原形動詞）作受詞，故選 to make。

grammar.q: ___ Jack had never cooked before, he decided to try his best.
grammar.ex: 句意為「雖然…但…」的對比關係，須用 Although 引導讓步子句。

grammar.q: Mia and Jack ___ have basketball practice because it was raining heavily.
grammar.ex: 表示過去因下雨而「不能」進行練習，須用 could not（couldn't）。

grammar.q: "You ___ become a great chef someday," Mia said with a smile.
grammar.ex: 表示對未來不確定的「或許」可能性，須用情態動詞 might。

vocab.q: If it rains a lot, we can say it is raining ___.
vocab.ex: heavily 意指「猛烈地、大量地」，符合句意「下很大的雨」。

vocab.q: A soft mixture of flour and water used to make bread or dumplings is called ___.
vocab.ex: dough 意指「麵團」，是麵粉與水混合而成的軟材料。

vocab.q: To cut food into small pieces is to ___ it.
vocab.ex: chop 意指「切碎」，符合句意「把食物切成小塊」。

vocab.q: To say something is true, even if it feels a little embarrassing, is to ___ it.
vocab.ex: admit 意指「承認」，符合句意「即使有點不好意思也說出真話」。

vocab.q: To cook food using hot water vapor is to ___ it.
vocab.ex: steam 意指「蒸」，指用熱蒸氣烹煮食物。
